subject: Reservation playbook & close milestones — Dedicated/Private GPU pool sizing
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam@helix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-18T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Draft reservation playbook + initial ask for lead-time constraints

Sam — following up from yesterday's demo. Attached is a short draft "reservation playbook" that lays out a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for evaluation -> PO -> reservation. High level: evaluation (2-3 weeks), production pilot (4–6 weeks), reserved capacity commit (quarterly/annual).

Two asks for you so we can lock the timeline:
1) Procurement lead-time constraints (internal approval windows, PO processing cadence)
2) Any hard constraints on in-region GPU placement (need for single-tenant on-prem vs VPC in us-west2)

I've penciled two pool-sizing options in the attachment: a conservative 8-GPU pool for pilot, and a 32-GPU reserve for scale. These map to our Dedicated and Private deployment patterns — see tab "sizing".

If you can confirm procurement timing and whether you prefer Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pools) vs Private (customer-hosted VPC/on-prem) we can convert this into the MAP timeline and DocuSign-ready SOW.

Thanks —
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: map-proposal-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Sam Carter <sam@helix.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@helix.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft reservation playbook + initial ask for lead-time constraints

Thanks Nikhil — reviewed quickly with the infra and procurement leads. A few constraints to call out: 
- Procurement: standard PO cycle is 3–4 weeks once SOW is finalized (we need finance sign-off).
- Hardware placement: For now we prefer Redwood Dedicated in us-west2 (data residency + managed pools) — on-prem option is possible but likely later in 2027.
- Evaluation: we can commit two weeks of evaluation, stretching to three if we need longer metrics collection.

Question: what are actual lead times for firing up a 32-GPU dedicated pool vs an 8-GPU pilot? If the 32-GPU path requires procurement lead-time similar to on-prem hardware, we may prefer a staged approach (pilot -> reserved 16 -> full 32).

Sam
CTO, Helix AI

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam@helix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft reservation playbook + initial ask for lead-time constraints

Sam — thanks, helpful. Short answers then a proposed MAP milestone table below.

Lead times (typical):
- 8-GPU Dedicated pilot (Redwood-managed): provisioning + warm-up = 3–5 business days (if no special network changes).
- 16–32 GPU Dedicated reserve (reserved capacity contract): 2–4 weeks if we need capacity commitments and specific instance types; 4–6 weeks if we require on-site networking approvals or private interconnect setup.
- Private (on-prem): depends on customer procurement for hardware and local ops — typically 8–12 weeks from PO to stable run.

Proposed MAP milestones (compressed for your 3-week evaluation preference):
1) Day 0: Sign provisional MAP (non-binding) — start evaluation runbook.
2) Day 1–14: Evaluation (we'll provide dedicated 8-GPU pilot pool and evaluation scripts, telemetry hooks to Console + token-level cost).
3) Day 10: Technical checkpoint — perf/latency/throughput review with SEs.
4) Day 14–21: Production pilot ramp (expand to 16 GPUs in Dedicated if metrics look good).
5) Day 21–35: Finalize reserved capacity sizing and sign SOW/PO for 16–32 GPU pool (Reserved Dedicated).

Sizing guidance rationale: the pilot (8 GPUs) covers a 50 RPS mixed chat/generation workload with 4–8k token contexts; 16 GPUs doubles concurrency (burst headroom for production pilot); 32 GPUs is prudent for business-critical rolling production. Marissa can add perf numbers in the next message.

Next steps: if you confirm pilot dates we can create a DocuSign SOW and a procurement checklist for your finance team. I've attached a condensed RFQ template for procurement.

- Nikhil

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam@helix.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft reservation playbook + initial ask for lead-time constraints

Sam — adding technical sizing detail from our infra bench runs so you have concrete numbers for the MAP and eval plan. TL;DR: the capacity bands below assume mixed workload (65% chat, 35% long-context generation):

- 8-GPU pilot (A100 80GB equiv): ~45–55 concurrent chat sessions at median latency < 300ms; token throughput ~120k tokens/min when batching is enabled.
- 16-GPU ramp: ~100 concurrent sessions; headroom for scheduled batch jobs and short high-throughput periods.
- 32-GPU reserve: designed for 400–600k tokens/min sustained with KV cache reuse and prefix caching.

Evaluation plan specifics (what we supply):
- Prebuilt eval harness (k6 + custom prompt set) and perf dashboards in Console.
- Cost/latency baseline report at Day 7 and Day 14.
- Failure injection scenario (region failover) during pilot to validate fallback policies.

Attachment: helix-msp-rfq.pdf (procurement-friendly RFQ stub).

If you want, we can start the pilot next Monday and I'll schedule the perf runs to give you Day 7 metrics for your internal review.

— Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Carter <sam@helix.ai>

All — this looks good and actionable. We approve the staged path: start 8-GPU Dedicated pilot next Monday, review Day 7 metrics, and target a PO for a 16 GPU reserved pool by end of January (finance needs the RFQ + SOW for approvals).

Please prepare a concise procurement packet (SOW, RFQ, sample PO language, estimated monthly run-rate for 16 GPUs). Also include the DocuSign-ready SOW as discussed. Procurement will review once they have those docs.

Sam
